functions.name: ApplyTheme
functions.documentation: Applies a theme to the current application UI. This method should be called when all windows are closed, in order for windows and controls to take effect.

params.name: theme
params.description: A string whose value is the theme name (or theme path and name) you want to apply to the current application. The theme path is optional. If not specified, the default value is "%AppeonInstallPath%\PowerBuilder [version]\IDE\theme" when the app is run from the IDE (at the development environment), and the default value is the "theme" under the root of the application installation directory when the application's executable file is run (at the production environment). If specified, it can be an absolute path or a relative path; and cannot be a UNC path (for example, "\\172.16.0.1\theme\Flat Design Blue" is unsupported). The relative path is relative to the PBT file at the development environment; and relative to the root of the installation directory of the app's executable file at the production environment. The theme name should be the sub-folder name under the specified theme path or the default path that contain the files for the theme, therefore the sub-folder name represents the theme name. In Windows system, the maximum length for a path is defined as 260 characters. Therefore, it is recommended the theme path (including theme name) should be less than 260 characters and the path alone (excluding theme name) should be less than 200 characters.

params.name: mdiframe
params.description: The name of an MDI frame window.

params.name: arrangetype
params.description: A value of the ArrangeTypes enumerated datatype specifying how you want the open sheets arranged in the MDI frame window. Values are: Cascade! -- Cascade the sheets that are not minimized so that each sheet's title bar is visible and arrange icons of minimized sheets in a row at the bottom of the frame. Layer! -- Layer the sheets that are not minimized so that each sheet completely covers the one below it and arrange icons of minimized sheets in a row at the bottom of the frame. Tile! -- Tile the sheets that are not minimized so that they do not overlap and arrange icons of minimized sheets in a row at the bottom of the frame. TileHorizontal! -- Tile the sheets that are not minimized so that each is beside the other without overlapping and arrange icons of minimized sheets in a row at the bottom of the frame. Icons! -- Arrange the minimized sheets in a row at the bottom of the frame.

functions.name: CloudAppGet
functions.documentation: Gets the settings (such as pictures loaded via URL or deployment version, DataWindow SQLPreview, HTTP request header etc.) of the application deployed by PowerClient or PowerServer.
functions.syntax: Integer CloudAppGet (string n, ref string v)

params.name: n
params.description: The name of the setting that is case insensitive. The setting can be: picturecachepath -- The directory where pictures are cached after downloaded from Web. The default value is "/picturecache". The leading forward slash (/ or //) indicates the root of the current application directory. Both the relative path and absolute path are supported. The path can also contain the system environment variable such as %appdata%\picturecache. clearpicturecacheonclose -- Whether to delete pictures from the cache directory when the application is closed. checkpictureforupdate -- Whether to check updates for the existing pictures. If pictures on Web have been updated, they will be downloaded again to the cache directory, otherwise, the picture in the cache directory will be used. The file size of the picture on Web will be obtained and compared with the file size of the picture in the cache directory. If the size is different, it indicates the picture has been updated on Web, and the picture will be downloaded again to the cache directory. deploymentversion -- The deployment version number of the application deployed by PowerClient or PowerServer. enablesqlpreview -- Whether to fully or partially support DataWindow SQLPreview, considering the tradeoff with performance under the PowerServer architecture. multipartformdataminsize -- The HTTP request header ( multipart/form-data or application/json ) in the PowerServer calls.

params.name: v
params.description: The value of the setting that is obtained.

functions.name: CloudAppSet
functions.documentation: Configures various settings for the application deployed by PowerClient or PowerServer, such as pictures loaded via URL, DataWindow SQLPreview support, HTTP request header etc.

params.name: n
params.description: The name of the setting that is case insensitive. The setting can be: picturecachepath -- The directory where pictures are cached after downloaded from Web. The default value is "/picturecache". The leading forward slash (/ or //) indicates the root of the current application directory. Both the relative path and absolute path are supported. The path can also contain the system environment variable such as %appdata%\picturecache. clearpicturecacheonclose -- Whether to delete pictures from the cache directory when the application is closed. checkpictureforupdate -- Whether to check updates for the existing pictures. If pictures on Web have been updated, they will be downloaded again to the cache directory, otherwise, the picture in the cache directory will be used. The file size of the picture on Web will be obtained and compared with the file size of the picture in the cache directory. If the size is different, it indicates the picture has been updated on Web, and the picture will be downloaded again to the cache directory. enablesqlpreview -- Whether to fully or partially support DataWindow SQLPreview. When fully supporting DataWindow SQLPreview, the performance may be compromised under the PowerServer architecture. When the "enablesqlpreview" setting is "false", the sqltype parameter supports PreviewSelect only and the request argument supports PreviewFunctionRetrieve only. The support for SQLPreview event is limited (the sqltype parameter does not support Previewlnsert, PreviewDelete, & PreviewUpdate; and the request argument does not support PreviewFunctionReselectRow and PreviewFunctionUpdate). When the "enablesqlpreview" setting is "true", the sqltype parameter supports PreviewSelect, Previewlnsert, PreviewDelete, & PreviewUpdate; and the request argument supports PreviewFunctionRetrieve, PreviewFunctionReselectRow, and PreviewFunctionUpdate. The SQLPreview event is fully supported; however, the performance may be compromised. When "enablesqlpreview" is "true", DataWindow Update uses the line-by-line commit approach (for each line of code, a separate request is sent to the server) rather than committing the entire DataWindow data to the server in one request, therefore, in the PowerServer architecture, the performance is easily affected by the network. If there is batch data update in the DataWindow, it is recommended to set "enablesqlpreview" to "false". By default, the "enablesqlpreview" setting is "false". You can consider setting "enablesqlpreview" to "true" for only some DataWindow Updates. Here is a code example: //Enable SQLPreview support before update, and then disable it after update. CloudAppSet ("enablesqlpreview", "true") if dw_1.update() = 1 then commit; else rollback; end if CloudAppSet ("enablesqlpreview", "false") multipartformdataminsize -- Uses the multipart/form-data header or application/json header when sending HTTP request to PowerServer. Choosing the appropriate header based on the data being sent ensures that your requests are correctly formatted and can be effectively processed by the server. Note All of the PowerServer HTTP request types support multipart/form-data , except the following: ValidationData and VerificationFailed. Use application/json when you need to send structured data, such as objects or arrays. This format is ideal for PowerServer Web APIs which expects JSON, as it allows for easier parsing and processing on the server side. By default, application/json is used. Use multipart/form-data (by setting "multipartformdataminsize" to "0" or any positive value) when you need to send large structured data, blobs, or files or a combination of them in a single request. This format is particularly useful for scenarios where network conditions are poor or slow, and you need to send substantial amounts of data to PowerServer (for example, for batch updates or UpdateBlob operations). When multipart/form-data is used, data will be compressed when sending requests from the client PC to PowerServer, to reduce network transmission time. However, keep in mind that this process requires additional resources in the client PC and PowerServer for compressing and decompressing the data. Please carefully consider the benefits and trade-offs when choosing this format.

params.name: v
params.description: The value of the setting to be set. When the name of the setting is "picturecachepath", the value can be a directory. When the name of the setting is "clearpicturecacheonclose", this value can be "true" or "false". When the name of the setting is "checkpictureforupdate", this value can be "true" or "false". When the name of the setting is "enablesqlpreview", this value can be "true" or "false". When the name of the setting is "multipartformdataminsize", this value can be 0, -1, or any positive value. 0 -- Uses the multipart/form-data header in all requests. -1 -- (Default) Uses the application/json header in all requests. any positive value -- Uses the multipart/form-data header only when the data in the request is larger than the specified size (in KB), for example, 128.

params.name: rtename
params.description: The name of the DataWindow control, DataStore object, or RichTextEdit control from which you want to copy the selection in rich text format. The DataWindow object in the DataWindow control or DataStore must be a RichText DataWindow.

params.name: selected
params.description: A boolean value indicated whether to copy selected text only. Values are: TRUE -- (Default) Copy selected text only FALSE -- Copy the entire contents of the band

params.name: band
params.description: A value of the Band enumerated datatype specifying the band from which to copy text. Values are: Detail! -- Copy text from the detail band Header! -- Copy text from the header band Footer! -- Copy text from the footer band The default is the band that contains the insertion point.

functions.name: Cos
functions.documentation: Calculates the cosine of an angle.

params.name: n
params.description: The angle (in radians) for which you want the cosine

functions.name: Cpu

functions.name: CreateDirectory

params.name: directoryname
params.description: String for the name of the directory you want to create

functions.name: CreateInstance
functions.documentation: Creates an instance of a component running on the COM+ server. This function is called from within a component instance running on COM+. Creates an instance of the .NET class and associates it with the DotNetObject object. The DotNetObject object must be instantiated first. The instance of the class can be used to access the functions/properties in the corresponding .NET class.

params.name: transactionserver
params.description: Reference to the TransactionServer service instance.

params.name: objectvariable
params.description: A global, instance, or local variable whose datatype is the same class as the object being created or an ancestor of that class.

params.name: classname
params.description: A string whose value is the name of the class datatype to be created. For COM+ components, you can optionally prepend a ProgID followed by a period to the class name (for example, "PowerBuilder.HTMLDataWindow".

params.name: objectname
params.description: Reference to the DotNetAssembly object instance.

params.name: DotNetObject
params.description: The name of the DotNetObject object.

The .NET constructor argument. Constructor argument is optional. If no argument is passed in, the application will automatically call the constructor that takes no parameter; and if there is no such parameterless constructor, the instance will fail to create.

functions.name: CreateJsonArray
functions.documentation: Creates the array of JsonArrayItem type as root item to initialize instance.

params.name: objectname
params.description: Reference to the JSONGenerator object instance.

functions.name: CreateJsonObject
functions.documentation: Creates the object of JsonObjectItem type as root item to initialize instance.

params.name: objectname
params.description: Reference to the JSONGenerator object instance.

functions.name: CreatePage
functions.documentation: Creates a tab page if it has not already been created.

params.name: userobject
params.description: The name of the tab page you want to create

functions.name: Cut
functions.returnType: Integer for DataWindow, InkEdit, and list boxes, Long for other controls
functions.documentation: Deletes selected text or an OLE object from the specified control and stores it on the clipboard, replacing the clipboard contents with the deleted text or object.

params.name: controlname
params.description: The name of the DataWindow, InkEdit, MultiLineEdit, SingleLineEdit, RichTextEdit, DropDownListBox, DropDownPictureListBox, or OLE control containing the text or object to be cut. If controlname is a DataWindow, text is cut from the edit control over the current row and column. If controlname is a DropDownListBox or DropDownPictureListBox, the AllowEdit property must be true.

functions.name: DataCount
functions.documentation: Reports the number of data points in the specified series in a graph.

params.name: controlname
params.description: The name of the graph in which you want the number of data points in a specific series, or the name of the DataWindow control or DataStore containing the graph

params.name: graphcontrol
params.description: The name of the graph in the DataWindow control or DataStore for which you want the data point count for the series

params.name: seriesname
params.description: A string whose value is the name of the series for which you want the number of data points

functions.name: DataSource
functions.documentation: Allows a RichTextEdit control to share data with a DataWindow and display the data in its input fields. If there are input fields in the RichTextEdit control that match the names of columns in the DataWindow, the data in the DataWindow is assigned to those input fields. The document in the RichTextEdit control is repeated so that there is an instance of the document for each row in the DataWindow.

params.name: rtename
params.description: The name of the RichTextEdit control for which you want to get data in a DataWindow

params.name: dwsource
params.description: The name of the DataWindow control, DataStore, or child DataWindow that contains the data to be connected with input fields in rtename

functions.name: Date
functions.documentation: Converts DateTime, string, or numeric data to data of type date or extracts a date value from a blob. You can use one of several syntaxes, depending on the datatype of the source data.

params.name: datetime
params.description: A DateTime value or a blob in which the first value is a date or DateTime value. The rest of the contents of the blob is ignored. Datetime can also be an Any variable containing a DateTime or blob.

params.name: string
params.description: A string containing a valid date (such as January 1, 2002, or 12-31-99) that you want returned as a date. Datetime can also be an Any variable containing a string.

params.name: year
params.description: The 4-digit year (1 to 9999) of the date

params.name: month
params.description: The 1- or 2-digit integer for the month (1 to 12) of the year

params.name: day
params.description: The 1- or 2-digit integer for the day (1 to 31) of the month

functions.name: DateTime
functions.documentation: Manipulates DateTime values. There are three syntaxes.

params.name: date
params.description: A value of type date.

params.name: time
params.description: A value of type time. If you omit time, PowerBuilder sets time to 00:00:00.000000 (midnight). If you specify time, only the hour portion is required.

params.name: blob
params.description: A blob in which the first value is a DateTime value. The rest of the contents of the blob is ignored. Blob can also be an Any variable containing a blob.

params.name: string
params.description: A string containing a valid datetime.

functions.name: Day
functions.documentation: Obtains the day of the month in a date value.

params.name: date
params.description: A date value from which you want the day

functions.name: DayName
functions.documentation: Determines the day of the week in a date value and returns the weekday's name.

params.name: date
params.description: A date value for which you want the name of the day

functions.name: DayNumber
functions.documentation: Determines the day of the week of a date value and returns the number of the weekday.

params.name: date
params.description: The date value from which you want the number of the day of the week

functions.name: DaysAfter
functions.documentation: Determines the number of days one date occurs after another.

params.name: date1
params.description: A date value that is the start date of the interval being measured

params.name: date2
params.description: A date value that is the end date of the interval

functions.name: DBHandle

params.name: transactionobject

params.name: stringorblob

functions.name: DeleteCategory

params.name: controlname

functions.name: DeleteCheckBox

params.name: controlname
params.description: The name of the RibbonBar control.

params.name: ItemHandle
params.description: The handle of the check box you want to delete.

params.name: listboxname
params.description: The name of the ListBox, DropDownListBox, PictureListBox, DropDownPictureListBox, or RibbonComboBoxItem from which you want to delete an item

params.name: index
params.description: The position number of the item you want to delete

params.name: listviewname
params.description: The name of the ListView control from which you want to delete an item

params.name: treeviewname
params.description: The name of the TreeView control from which you want to delete an item

params.description: The handle of the item you want to delete

params.description: The name of the RibbonMenu control from which you want to delete an item

params.description: The index of the menu item (RibbonMenuItem) whose submenu you want to delete. If not specified, the menu item will be deleted; if specified to a valid value, the submenu of the menu item (whose index is ParentIndex) will be deleted; if specified to an invalid value, an error would occur and this operation would return -1.

functions.name: DeleteItems

params.description: The name of the ListView control from which you want to delete all items

params.description: The name of the RibbonBar control.

params.name: ItemHandle
params.description: The handle of the large button you want to delete.

params.name: listviewname
params.description: The name of the ListView control to which you want to delete a large picture from the image list

params.name: index
params.description: The index entry for the large picture you want to delete

params.name: controlname
params.description: The name of the RibbonApplicationMenu control from which you want to remove the master menu item.

params.name: ParentIndex
params.description: The index of the master menu item (RibbonMenuItem) whose submenu you want to delete. If not specified, the master menu item will be deleted; if specified to a valid value, the submenu item of the master menu item (whose index is ParentIndex) will be deleted; if specified to an invalid value, an error would occur and this operation would return -1.

params.name: Index
params.description: The index of the master menu item or submenu item which you want to delete. If index is invalid, an error would occur and this operation would return -1.

functions.name: DeletePanel

params.name: controlname
params.description: The name of the RibbonBar control.

params.name: ItemHandle
params.description: The handle of the panel you want to delete.

functions.name: DeletePicture

params.name: controlname

params.description: The index of the recent menu item which you want to delete.

params.description: A string whose value is the name of the series you want to delete from controlname

functions.name: DeleteSmallButton

params.description: The name of the RibbonBar control.

params.description: The handle of the small button you want to delete.

functions.name: DeleteSmallPicture

params.name: listviewname
params.description: The name of the ListView control from which you want to delete a small picture from the image list

params.name: index
params.description: The index number of the small picture you want to delete

params.description: The name of the ListView control from which you want to delete all small pictures

params.name: index
params.description: The index number of the state picture you want to delete

params.description: The name of the ListView or TreeView control from which you want to delete all state pictures

params.description: The handle of the tab button you want to delete.

params.description: Instance name of the Profiling or TraceTree object

functions.name: DirectoryExists
functions.returnType: Returns true if the directory exists
functions.documentation: Determines if the named directory exists.

params.name: directoryname
params.description: String for the name of the directory you want to verify as existing

functions.name: DirList
functions.documentation: Populates a ListBox with a list of files. You can specify a path, a mask, and a file type to restrict the set of files displayed. If the window has an associated StaticText control, DirList can display the current drive and directory as well.

params.name: listboxname
params.description: The name of the ListBox control you want to populate.

params.name: filespec
params.description: A string whose value is the file pattern. This is usually a mask (for example, *.INI or *.TXT). If you include a path, it becomes the current drive and directory.

params.name: filetype
params.description: An unsigned integer representing one or more types of files you want to list in the ListBox. Types are: 0 -- Read/write files 1 -- Read-only files 2 -- Hidden files 4 -- System files 16 -- Subdirectories 32 -- Archive (modified) files 16384 -- Drives 32768 -- Exclude read/write files from the list To list several types, add the numbers associated with the types. For example, to list read-write files, subdirectories, and drives, use 0+16+16384 or 16400 for filetype.

params.name: statictext
params.description: The name of the StaticText in which you want to display the current drive and directory.

functions.name: DirSelect
functions.documentation: When a ListBox has been populated with the DirList function, DirSelect retrieves the current selection and stores it in a string variable.

params.name: listboxname
params.description: The name of the ListBox control from which you want to retrieve the current selection. The ListBox must have been populated using DirList, and the selection must be a drive letter, a file, or the name of a directory.

params.name: selection
params.description: A string variable in which the selected path name will be put.

functions.name: Disable
functions.documentation: Disables an item on a menu. The menu item is dimmed (its color is changed to the user's disabled text color, usually gray), and the user cannot select it.

params.name: menuname
params.description: The name of the menu selection you want to deactivate (disable)

functions.name: DisableCommit
functions.documentation: Declares that a component's transaction updates are inconsistent and cannot be committed in their present state.

params.name: transactionserver
params.description: Reference to the TransactionServer service instance

functions.name: DisconnectObject
functions.documentation: Releases any object that is connected to the specified OLEObject variable.

params.name: oleobject
params.description: The name of an OLEObject variable that you want to disconnect from an OLE object. You cannot specify an OLEObject that is the Object property of an OLE control.

functions.name: DisconnectServer
functions.documentation: Disconnects a client application from a server application.

params.name: connection
params.description: The name of the Connection object used to establish the connection you want to delete

functions.name: Double
functions.documentation: Converts a string to a double or obtains a double value that is stored in a blob.

params.name: stringorblob
params.description: A string whose value you want returned as a double or a blob in which the first value is the double value. The rest of the contents of the blob is ignored. Stringorblob can also be an Any variable containing a double or blob.

functions.name: DoVerb
functions.documentation: Requests the OLE server application to execute the specified verb for the OLE object in an OLE control or OLE DWObject.

params.name: objectref
params.description: The name of the OLE control or the fully qualified name of a OLE DWObject within a DataWindow control for which you want to execute a verb. The fully qualified name for a DWObject has this syntax: dwcontrol.Object.dwobjectname

params.name: verb
params.description: An integer identifying a verb known to the OLE server application. Verbs are operations that the server can perform on the OLE object. Check the documentation for the server's OLE implementation to find out what verbs it supports.

functions.name: Drag
functions.documentation: Starts or ends the dragging of a control.

params.name: control
params.description: The name of the control you want to drag or stop dragging

params.name: dragmodes
params.description: A value of the DragMode datatype indicating the action you want to take on control: Begin! -- Put control in drag mode Cancel! -- Stop dragging control but do not cause a DragDrop event End! -- Stop dragging control and if control is over a target object, cause a DragDrop event

functions.name: DraggedObject
functions.returnType: DragObject, a special datatype that includes all draggable controls (all the controls but
functions.documentation: Returns a reference to the control that triggered a drag event.

functions.name: Draw
functions.documentation: Draws a picture control at a specified location in the current window.

params.name: picture
params.description: The name of the picture control you want to draw in the current window

params.name: xlocation
params.description: The x coordinate of the location (in PowerBuilder units) at which you want to draw the picture

params.name: ylocation
params.description: The y coordinate of the location (in PowerBuilder units) at which you want to draw the picture

functions.name: EditLabel

params.description: The ListView control in which you want to enable label editing

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the ListView item to be edited

params.name: treeviewname
params.description: The TreeView control in which you want to enable label editing

params.name: itemhandle
params.description: The handle of the item to be edited

functions.name: Enable

params.description: Reference to the TransactionServer service instance

functions.documentation: Enables the database secure connection. This function takes effect only when the application is deployed via the Application project and the PowerClient project (it returns -1 when the application is deployed via the PowerServer project).

params.name: transaction
params.description: The name of a connected transaction object.

params.name: flag
params.description: A boolean indicating whether to enable the secure connection: True -- Enables the secure connection. False -- Not to enable the secure connection.

functions.name: EndMerge
functions.documentation: Indicates the merge mode stops and requests will be submitted immediately. This function takes effect only when the application is deployed via the PowerServer project (it will be ignored when the application is deployed via the PowerClient project or the Application project).

params.name: objectname
params.description: The name of the PowerServerLabel object.

functions.name: EntryList

params.name: instancename
params.description: Instance name of the TraceTree object.

params.name: list
params.description: An unbounded array variable of datatype TraceTreeNode in which EntryList stores a TraceTreeNode object for each top-level entry in the trace tree model. This argument is passed by reference.

functions.name: EvaluateJavascriptAsync
functions.documentation: Executes JavaScript asynchronously. This function triggers the EvaluateJavascriptFinished event.

params.name: controlname
params.description: The name of the WebBrowser control.

params.name: script
params.description: The JavaScript to be evaluated.

functions.name: EvaluateJavascriptSync
functions.documentation: Executes JavaScript synchronously.
functions.syntax: controlname.EvaluateJavascriptSync (string script{, ref string result{, ref string error}})

params.name: controlname
params.description: The name of the WebBrowser control.

params.name: script
params.description: The JavaScript to be evaluated. The JavaScript cannot have statements that show dialog boxes. If a dialog box must be displayed in JavaScript, the script must be executed asynchronously. If there are multiple JavaScript statements, only the last JavaScript statement will have its result returned.

params.name: result
params.description: The result of script execution. The execution result is represented in a JSON string. The supported JavaScript data types are bool, int, double, string, date, array. When the above types are mapped to the PowerBuilder data types, they are boolean, integer, double, string, datetime, array. For example, {"type":"double","value":1585620350123}; //returns a double-type value {"type":"string","value":"12d6_1585674123456_74563"}; //returns a string-type value

params.name: error
params.description: The error information if an error occurs during execution. The error information is represented in a JSON string. For example, {"type":"error","value":"Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'style' "}

functions.name: ExecRemote

params.name: command
params.description: A string whose value is the command you want a DDE server application to execute. To determine the correct command format, see the documentation for the server application.

params.name: applname
params.description: A string whose value is the DDE name of the server application.

params.name: topicname
params.description: A string identifying the data or the instance of the DDE application you want to use with the command. In Microsoft Excel, for example, the topic name could be system or the name of an open spreadsheet.

params.name: handle
params.description: A long that identifies the channel to the DDE server application. The OpenChannel function returns handle when you call it to open a DDE channel.

params.name: windowhandle
params.description: The handle to the window that you want to act as the DDE client. Specify this parameter to control which window is acting as the DDE client when you have more than one open window. If you do not specify windowhandle, the active window acts as the DDE client.

params.description: Character encoding of the file to which the data is saved. If you do not specify an encoding parameter, the file is saved in UTF8 format. Values are: EncodingANSI! EncodingUTF8! (default) EncodingUTF16LE! EncodingUTF16BE!

params.description: The name of the RibbonBar control.

params.name: objectname
params.description: The name of the ExtractorObject object.

params.name: source
params.description: A string whose value is the full directory of the compressed archive. Or a blob whose value is the compressed data stream.

params.name: items[]
params.description: The specified files (or folders) to extract. The files (or folders) can be obtained through GetFilesList . If you specify a single file in a subfolder, the method will create the whole folder structure to the file on target.

params.name: item
params.description: The specified file to extract. You can only extract one file (cannot be multiple files or a folder) into a blob.

params.name: target
params.description: A string whose value is the directory where the compressed archive will be extracted. The existing files with the same name on target will be overwritten. Or a blob where the decompression results will be stored.

params.name: format
params.description: A value of the enumerated datatype ArchiveFormat specifying the format of the source file. Values are: ArchiveFormatZIP!: zip file. This is the default value. ArchiveFormat7Zip!: 7zip file. File size of 7zip file may not be obtained correctly during extraction. ArchiveFormatRAR!: rar file. ArchiveFormatGZip!: gzip format archive. ArchiveFormatTAR!: tar format archive. ArchiveFormatLZMA!: lzma format archive. ArchiveFormatLZMA86!: lzma86 format archive.

params.name: destFilePath
params.description: The path to save the attachment(s). The path will be auto created if it does not exist.

params.name: destFilePath
params.description: The path and file name to save the attachment as.

functions.name: Fact
functions.documentation: Determines the factorial of a number.

params.name: n
params.description: The number for which you want the factorial

functions.name: FileClose
functions.documentation: Closes the file associated with the specified file number. The file number was assigned to the file with the FileOpen function.

params.name: file#
params.description: The integer assigned to the file you want to close. The FileOpen function returns the file number when it opens the file.

functions.name: FileCopy
functions.documentation: Copies one file to another, optionally overwriting the target file.

params.name: sourcefile
params.description: String for the name of the file you want to copy

params.name: targetfile
params.description: String for the name of the file you are copying to

params.name: replace
params.description: Boolean specifying whether to replace the target file (true) or not (false)

functions.name: FileDelete
functions.documentation: Deletes the named file.

params.name: filename
params.description: A string whose value is the name of the file you want to delete

functions.name: FileEncoding
functions.returnType: A value of the enumerated datatype encoding
functions.documentation: Checks the encoding of the specified file.

params.name: filename
params.description: The name of the file you want to test for encoding type

functions.name: FileExists
functions.documentation: Reports whether the specified file exists.

params.name: filename
params.description: A string whose value is the name of a file

functions.name: FileLength
functions.documentation: Reports the length of a file whose size does not exceed 2GB in bytes.

params.name: filename
params.description: A string whose value is the name of the file for which you want to know the length. If filename is not on the current application library search path, you must specify the fully qualified name.

functions.name: FileLength64
functions.documentation: Reports the length of a file of any size in bytes.

params.name: filename
params.description: A string whose value is the name of the file for which you want to know the length. If filename is not on the current application library search path, you must specify the fully qualified name.

functions.name: FileMove
functions.documentation: Moves a file.

params.name: sourcefile
params.description: String for the name of the file you want to move

params.name: targetfile
params.description: String for the name of the location you are moving the file

functions.name: FileOpen
functions.documentation: Opens the specified file for reading or writing and assigns it a unique integer file number. You use this integer to identify the file when you read, write, or close the file. The optional arguments filemode, fileaccess, filelock, and writemode determine the mode in which the file is opened.
functions.syntax: FileOpen ( filename {, filemode {, fileaccess {, filelock {, writemode {, encoding }}}}} )

params.name: filename
params.description: A string whose value is the name of the file you want to open. If filename is not on the current directory's relative search path, you must enter the fully qualified name.

params.name: filemode
params.description: A value of the FileMode enumerated type that specifies how the end of a file read or file write is determined. Values are: LineMode! -- (Default) Read or write the file a line at a time StreamMode! -- Read blocks of binary data TextMode! -- Read text blocks For more information, see Usage below.

params.name: fileaccess
params.description: A value of the FileAccess enumerated type that specifies whether the file is opened for reading or writing. Values are: Read! -- (Default) Read-only access Write! -- Write-only access If PowerBuilder does not find the file, a new file is created if the fileaccess argument is set to Write!

params.name: filelock
params.description: A value of the FileLock enumerated type specifying whether others have access to the opened file. Values are: LockReadWrite! -- (Default) Only the user who opened the file has access LockRead! -- Only the user who opened the file can read it, but everyone has write access LockWrite! -- Only the user who opened the file can write to it, but everyone has read access Shared! -- All users have read and write access.

params.name: writemode
params.description: A value of the WriteMode enumerated datatype. When fileaccess is Write!, specifies whether existing data in the file is overwritten. Values are: Append! -- (Default) Write data to the end of the file Replace! -- Replace all existing data in the file Writemode is ignored if the fileaccess argument is Read!

params.name: encoding
params.description: Character encoding of the file you want to create. Specify this argument when you create a new text file using text or line mode. If you do not specify an encoding, the file is created with ANSI encoding. Values are: EncodingANSI! (default) EncodingUTF8! EncodingUTF16LE! EncodingUTF16BE!

functions.name: FileRead
functions.documentation: Reads data from the file associated with the specified file number, which was assigned to the file with the FileOpen function. FileRead is maintained for backward compatibility. Use the FileReadEx function for new development.

params.name: file#
params.description: The integer assigned to the file when it was opened

params.name: variable
params.description: The name of the string or blob variable into which you want to read the data

functions.name: FileReadEx
functions.documentation: Reads data from the file associated with the specified file number, which was assigned to the file with the FileOpen function.
functions.syntax: FileReadEx ( file#, blob {, length } ) FileReadEx ( file#, string )

params.name: file#
params.description: The integer assigned to the file when it was opened.

params.name: blob
params.description: The name of the string or blob variable into which you want to read the data.

params.name: length
params.description: In text or stream mode, the number of bytes a retrieve requires. The default value is the length of the file.

functions.name: FileSeek
functions.documentation: Moves the file pointer to the specified position in a file whose size does not exceed 2GB. The file pointer is the position in the file at which the next read or write begins.

params.name: file#
params.description: The integer assigned to the file when it was opened.

params.name: position
params.description: A long whose value is the new position of the file pointer relative to the position specified in origin, in bytes.

params.name: origin
params.description: The value of the SeekType enumerated datatype specifying where you want to start the seek. Values are: FromBeginning! -- (Default) At the beginning of the file FromCurrent! -- At the current position FromEnd! -- At the end of the file

functions.name: FileSeek64
functions.documentation: Moves the file pointer to the specified position in a file of any size. The file pointer is the position in the file at which the next read or write begins.

params.name: file#
params.description: The integer assigned to the file when it was opened.

params.name: position
params.description: A long whose value is the new position of the file pointer relative to the position specified in origin, in bytes.

params.name: origin
params.description: The value of the SeekType enumerated datatype specifying where you want to start the seek. Values are: FromBeginning! -- (Default) At the beginning of the file FromCurrent! -- At the current position FromEnd! -- At the end of the file

functions.name: FileWrite
functions.documentation: Writes data to the file associated with the specified file number. The file number was assigned to the file with the FileOpen function. FileWrite is maintained for backward compatibility. Use the FileWriteEx function for new development.

params.name: file#
params.description: The integer assigned to the file when the file was opened

params.name: variable
params.description: A string or blob whose value is the data you want to write to the file

functions.name: FileWriteEx
functions.documentation: Writes data to the file associated with the specified file number. The file number was assigned to the file with the FileOpen function.
functions.syntax: FileWriteEx ( file#, blob {, length }) FileWriteEx ( file#, string )

params.name: file#
params.description: The integer assigned to the file when the file was opened

params.name: blob
params.description: A blob or string whose value is the data you want to write to the file.

params.name: length
params.description: In text or stream mode, the number of bytes to be written. The default value is the length of the file.

functions.name: Fill
functions.documentation: Builds a string of the specified length by repeating the specified characters until the result string is long enough.

params.name: chars
params.description: A string whose value will be repeated to fill the return string

params.name: n
params.description: A long whose value is the length of the string you want returned

functions.name: FillA
functions.documentation: Builds a string of the specified length in bytes by repeating the specified characters until the result string is long enough.

params.name: chars
params.description: The string whose value is repeated to fill the return string

params.name: n
params.description: A long specifying the number of bytes in the return string

functions.name: FillW
functions.documentation: Builds a string of the specified length by repeating the specified characters until the result string is long enough. This function is obsolete. It has the same behavior as Fill in SBCS and DBCS environments.

functions.name: Find
functions.documentation: Finds data in a DataWindow control or DataStore, or text in a RichTextEdit control or RichTextEdit DataWindow or DataStore. You can specify search direction and whether to match whole words and case. Finds the specified text in the control and highlights the text if found. For syntax for DataWindows and DataStores, see the Find method for DataWindows in the section called “Find” in DataWindow Reference .
functions.syntax: controlname.Find ( searchtext, forward, insensitive, wholeword, cursor )

params.name: controlname
params.description: The name of the RichTextEdit, DataWindow control, or DataStore whose contents you want to search.

params.name: searchtext
params.description: A string whose value is the text you want to find. For the RichTextEdit control, searchtext is limited to 99 characters.

params.name: forward
params.description: A boolean value indicating the direction you want to search. Values are: TRUE -- The search proceeds forward from the cursor position or, if cursor is false, from the start of the document. FALSE -- The search proceeds backward from the cursor position or, if cursor is false, from the end of the document.

params.name: insensitive
params.description: A boolean value indicating the search string and the found text must match case. Values are: TRUE -- The search is not sensitive to case. FALSE -- The search is case-sensitive.

params.name: wholeword
params.description: A boolean value indicating that the found text must be a whole word. Values are: TRUE -- The found text must be a whole word. FALSE -- The found text can be a partial word.

params.name: cursor
params.description: A boolean value indicating where the search begins. Values are: TRUE -- The search begins at the cursor position. FALSE -- The search begins at the start of the document if forward is true or at the end if forward is false.

functions.name: FindCategory
functions.documentation: Obtains the number of a category in a graph when you know the category's label.

params.name: controlname
params.description: A string whose value is the name of the graph in which you want to find a specific category, or the name of the DataWindow control containing the graph.

params.name: graphcontrol
params.description: A string whose value is the name of the graph in the DataWindow control in which you want to find a specific category.

params.name: categoryvalue
params.description: A value that is the category for which you want the number. The value you specify must be the same datatype as the datatype of the category axis.

functions.name: FindClassDefinition
functions.documentation: Searches for an object in one or more PowerBuilder libraries (PBLs) and provides information about its class definition.

params.name: classname
params.description: The name of an object (also called a class or class definition) for which you want information.

params.name: librarylist
params.description: An array of strings whose values are the fully qualified pathnames of PBLs. If you omit librarylist, FindClassDefinition searches the library list associated with the running application.

functions.name: FindFunctionDefinition
functions.documentation: Searches for a global function in one or more PowerBuilder libraries (PBLs) and provides information about the script definition.

params.name: functionname
params.description: The name of a global function for which you want information.

params.name: librarylist
params.description: An array of strings whose values are the fully qualified pathnames of PBLs. If you omit librarylist, FindFunctionDefinition searches the library list associated with the running application.

functions.name: FindItem
functions.documentation: Finds the next item in a list.

params.name: listboxname
params.description: The name of the ListBox control in which you want to find an item.

params.name: text
params.description: A string whose value is the starting text of the item you want to find.

params.name: index
params.description: The number of the item just before the first item to be searched. To search the whole list, specify 0.

params.name: listviewname
params.description: The ListView control for which you want to search for items

params.name: startindex
params.description: The index number from which you want your search to begin

params.name: label
params.description: The string that is the target of the search

params.name: partial
params.description: If set to true, the search looks for a partial label match

params.name: wrap
params.description: If set to true, the search returns to the first index item after it has finished

params.name: direction
params.description: The direction in which to search. Values are: DirectionAll! DirectionUp! DirectionDown! DirectionLeft! DirectionRight!

params.name: focused
params.description: If set to true, the search looks for the next ListView item that has focus.

params.name: selected
params.description: If set to true, the search looks for the next ListView item that is selected.

params.name: cuthighlighted
params.description: If set to true, the search looks for the next ListView item that is the target of a cut operation.

params.name: drophighlighted
params.description: If set to true, the search looks for next ListView item that is the target of a drag and drop operation.

params.name: treeviewname
params.description: The name of the TreeView control in which you want to find a specified item.

params.name: navigationcode
params.description: A value of the TreeNavigation enumerated datatype specifying the relationship between itemhandle and the item you want to find. See the table in Usage note for a list of valid values.

params.name: itemhandle
params.description: A long for the handle of an item related via navigationcode to the item for which you are searching.

functions.name: FindMatchingFunction
functions.documentation: Finds out what function in a class matches a specified signature. The signature is a combination of a script name and an argument list.

params.name: classdefobject
params.description: The name of the ClassDefinition object describing the class in which you want to find a function.

params.name: scriptname
params.description: A string whose value is the name of the function.

params.name: argumentlist
params.description: An unbounded array of strings whose values are the datatypes of the function arguments. If the variable is passed by reference, the string must include "ref" before the datatype. If the variable is an array, you must include array brackets after the datatype. The format is: { ref } datatype { [] } For a bounded array, the argument must include the range, as in: ref integer[1 TO 10]

functions.name: FindNext
functions.documentation: Finds the next occurrence of text in the control and highlights it, using criteria set up in a previous call of the Find function.

params.name: controlname
params.description: The name of the RichTextEdit or DataWindow control whose contents you want to search

functions.name: FindSeries
functions.documentation: Obtains the number of a series in a graph when you know the series' name.

params.name: controlname
params.description: The name of the graph containing the series for which you want the number, or the name of the DataWindow control containing the graph

params.name: graphcontrol
params.description: A string whose value is the name of the graph in the DataWindow control containing the series

params.name: seriesname
params.description: A string whose value is the name of the series for which you want the number

functions.name: FindTypeDefinition
functions.documentation: Searches for a type in one or more PowerBuilder libraries (PBLs) and provides information about its type definition. You can also get type definitions for system types.

params.name: typename
params.description: The name of a simple datatype, enumerated datatype, or class for which you want information. To find a type definition for a nested type, use this form: libraryEntryName`typename

params.name: librarylist
params.description: An array of strings whose values are the fully qualified pathnames of PBLs. If you omit librarylist, FindTypeDefinition searches the library list associated with the running application. PowerBuilder also searches its own libraries for built-in definitions, such as enumerated datatypes and system classes.

functions.name: FormCheckBoxGetChecked
functions.documentation: Gets the checked status of the checkbox form field at the given field ID.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the checkbox form field.

functions.name: FormCheckBoxInsert
functions.documentation: Inserts a checkbox type form field at the current text input position in a RichTextEdit control. Users can click the checkbox form field to change the field value if necessary.
functions.syntax: rtename.FormCheckBoxInsert(boolean checked{, char checkedChar, char uncheckedChar})

params.name: checked
params.description: The status of the checkbox when it is initially inserted.

params.name: checkedChar
params.description: The character to show in the field if the checked status is true. You can only pass one character to the argument, for example, T.The default value is 0x25A0, which is .

params.name: uncheckedChar
params.description: The character to show in the fieldif the checked status is false. You can only pass one character to the argument, for example, T. The default value is 0x25A1, which is .

functions.name: FormCheckBoxSetChecked
functions.documentation: Sets the checked status of the checkbox form field at the given field ID.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the checkbox form field.

params.name: checked
params.description: The status that you want to set the checkbox field to.

functions.name: FormComboBoxGetItems
functions.documentation: Gets the list of items from the dropdown of a combobox field.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the combobox field.

params.name: items[]
params.description: The item options in the combobox dropdown that display when the user clicks at the combobox field.

functions.name: FormComboBoxInsert
functions.documentation: Inserts a combobox type form field at the current text input position in a RichTextEdit control. A combobox has a list of items in its dropdown and text in its edit field. After a combobox is inserted, the edit field shows the text. If a user clicks at the text, the combobox will display with the list of items.
functions.syntax: rtename.FormComboBoxInsert(string fieldText, string items[], boolean showDropDownArrow{, integer emptyWidth})

params.name: fieldText
params.description: The text that displays in the edit field of the combobox.

params.name: items[]
params.description: The item options to display in the combobox when the user clicks at the combobox field.

params.name: showDropDownArrow
params.description: The option that decides whether the combobox's dropdown arrow is immediately shown after insertion.

params.name: emptyWidth
params.description: The combobox's width, in twips, when its edit field is empty. If this parameter is omitted, a default width of 2000 twips is used. For almost all units of measurement in the RichTextEdit control, twips are used. Twip is a fabricated word meaning twentieth of a point (pt).

params.name: selectedIndex
params.description: The index of the item that displays in the edit field of the combobox. If the index is 0, the edit field is empty. If the index is n, the nth item in items[] displays in the edit field.

functions.name: FormComboBoxSetItems
functions.documentation: Sets the list of items to display for the dropdown of a combobox field.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the combobox field.

params.name: items[]
params.description: The item options in the combobox dropdown to display when the user clicks at the combobox field.

functions.name: FormDateFieldGetDate
functions.documentation: Gets the date value displayed in the date form field.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the date field.

functions.name: FormDateFieldGetFormat
functions.documentation: Gets the date format used for displaying the date in the date form field.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the date field.

functions.name: FormDateFieldInsert
functions.documentation: Inserts a date type form field at the current text input position in a RichTextEdit control. A date field shows a date in its edit field. After a date field is inserted, if a user clicks at the date, a date-picking control will display for selecting a different date.
functions.syntax: rtename.FormDateFieldInsert(date fieldDate, boolean showDateControl{ {,string format} {,integer emptyWidth}})

params.name: fieldDate
params.description: The date to display in the edit field. The user can changed this date through a date picking control. When this parameter does not contain a date, the new date field is empty.

params.name: showDateControl
params.description: Specifies whether the date picking control is immediately shown after insertion.

params.name: format
params.description: The format for displaying the date. When this parameter is omitted a default format is used depending on the language set for the date field's text.

params.name: emptyWidth
params.description: The combobox's width, in twips, when its edit field is empty. If this parameter is omitted, a default width of 2000 twips is used. For almost all units of measurement in the RichTextEdit control, twips are used. Twip is a fabricated word meaning twentieth of a point (pt).

functions.name: FormDateFieldSetDate
functions.documentation: Sets the date value to display in the date form field.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the date form field.

params.name: fieldDate
params.description: The date value to assign to the date form field.

functions.name: FormDateFieldSetFormat
functions.documentation: Sets the date format for displaying the date in the date form field.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the date field.

params.name: format
params.description: The date format to use for the field.

functions.name: FormFieldDelete
functions.documentation: Deletes the specified form field. The type of the form field may be FormFieldCheckBox, FormFieldComboBox, FormFieldText, and FormFieldDate.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the form field.

params.name: deleteTotal
params.description: True means deleting the field completely. False means changing the form field to plain text.

functions.name: FormFieldGetCurrent
functions.documentation: Gets the ID of the current form field. The type of the form field may be FormFieldCheckBox, FormFieldComboBox, FormFieldText, and FormFieldDate.

functions.name: FormFieldGetDeletable
functions.documentation: Gets the deletable setting of the specified form field. The type of the form field may be FormFieldCheckBox, FormFieldComboBox, FormFieldText, and FormFieldDate.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the form field.

functions.name: FormFieldGetEmptyWidth
functions.documentation: Gets the empty width (that is, the width of the field when there is no text displayed) set for a form field. The type of the form field may be FormFieldCheckBox, FormFieldComboBox, FormFieldText, and FormFieldDate.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the form field.

functions.name: FormFieldGetEnd
functions.documentation: Gets the end position of the specified form field. The type of the form field may be FormFieldCheckBox, FormFieldComboBox, FormFieldText, and FormFieldDate. The ending position is the character index (starting at 1) of the last character of the form field in the RichTextEdit control. If there are new line characters in the content, each new line character is counted as one character too. If the RichTextEdit control contains header and footer, the character indexes of the header, footer and main content are accumulated separately.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the form field.

functions.name: FormFieldGetStart
functions.documentation: Gets the starting position of the specified form field. The type of the form field may be FormFieldCheckBox, FormFieldComboBox, FormFieldText, and FormFieldDate. The starting position is the character index (starting at 1) of the first character of the form field in the RichTextEdit control. If there are new line characters in the content, each new line character is counted as one character too. If the RichTextEdit control contains header and footer, the character indexes of the header, footer and main content are accumulated separately.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the form field.

functions.name: FormFieldGetText
functions.documentation: Gets the text being displayed for a form field. The type of the form field may be FormFieldCheckBox, FormFieldComboBox, FormFieldText, and FormFieldDate.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the form field.

functions.name: FormFieldNext
functions.documentation: Finds the next form field after the specified form field. The type of the form field may be FormFieldCheckBox, FormFieldComboBox, FormFieldText, and FormFieldDate. You can specify which form field type to look for.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The ID of the form field based on which to search for the next field.

params.name: formFieldTypes
params.description: The form field types the function shall search for. If unspecified, the function will search for all the form field types, including FormFieldCheckBox, FormFieldComboBox, FormFieldText, and FormFieldDate.

functions.name: FormFieldSetCurrent
functions.documentation: Sets a form field as current. The type of the form field may be FormFieldCheckBox, FormFieldComboBox, FormFieldText, and FormFieldDate.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The ID assigned to the form field that shall be set as current.

functions.name: FormFieldSetDeletable
functions.documentation: Sets whether a form field is deletable by pressing the keyboard key. The type of the form field may be FormFieldCheckBox, FormFieldComboBox, FormFieldText, and FormFieldDate. When a form field is newly-inserted, it is deletable. If the deletable is set to false, it is not deletable by pressing the keyboard key, but can still be deletable by calling the corresponding delete function (for example, FormFieldDelete, or ClearAll),

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the form field.

params.name: deletable
params.description: Specifies whether the form field is deletable by pressing the keyboard key. True means deletable, and false means not deletable.

functions.name: FormFieldSetEmptyWidth
functions.documentation: Sets the empty width (that is, the width of the field when there is no text displayed) for a form field. The type of the form field may be FormFieldCheckBox, FormFieldComboBox, FormFieldText, and FormFieldDate.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the form field.

params.name: width
params.description: The width, in twips, when the form field is empty. If this parameter is omitted, a default width of 2000 twips is used. For almost all units of measurement in the RichTextEdit control, twips are used. Twip is a fabricated word meaning twentieth of a point (pt).

functions.name: FormFieldSetText
functions.documentation: Sets the display text for a form field. The type of the form field may be FormFieldCheckBox, FormFieldComboBox, FormFieldText, and FormFieldDate.

params.name: fieldID
params.description: The unique ID assigned to the form field.

params.name: text
params.description: The text to display for the form field.

functions.name: FormTextFieldInsert
functions.documentation: Inserts a text type form field at the current text input position in a RichTextEdit control. It is a text input field. If such a field is empty, it can be set to a specified width so that the users can see where to enter text.

params.name: text
params.description: The text to display in the text input field.

params.name: emptyWidth
params.description: The width of the field, in twips, when the field is empty. If this parameter is omitted, a default width of 2000 twips is used. For almost all units of measurement in the RichTextEdit control, twips are used. Twip is a fabricated word meaning twentieth of a point (pt).

functions.name: FromAnsi
functions.documentation: Converts a blob containing an ANSI character string to a Unicode string. This function is obsolete starting from PowerBuilder 10.

params.name: blob
params.description: A blob containing an ANSI character string you want to convert to a Unicode string

functions.name: FromUnicode
functions.documentation: Converts a blob containing a Unicode character string to a string in the file format of the current version of PowerBuilder. This function is obsolete starting from PowerBuilder 10.

params.name: blob
params.description: A blob containing a Unicode character string you want to convert to a string in the file format of the current version of PowerBuilder

functions.name: GarbageCollect
functions.documentation: Forces immediate garbage collection.

functions.name: GarbageCollectGetTimeLimit
functions.documentation: Gets the current minimum interval for garbage collection.

functions.name: GarbageCollectSetTimeLimit
functions.documentation: Sets the minimum interval between garbage collection passes.

params.name: newtimeinmilliseconds
params.description: A long (in milliseconds) that you want to set as the minimum period between garbage collection cycles. If null, the existing interval is not changed.

functions.name: GetAccessToken
functions.documentation: Gets the access token returned by the authorization server.

params.name: objectname
params.description: A reference to the TokenResponse object in which you want to get the access token.

functions.name: GetActiveCategory
functions.documentation: Gets the active category in the RibbonBar control.

params.name: controlname
params.description: The name of the RibbonBar control.

params.name: Item
params.description: A RibbonCategoryItem variable in which you want to store the active category.

functions.name: GetActiveSheet
functions.documentation: Returns the currently active sheet in an MDI frame window.

params.name: mdiframewindow
params.description: The MDI frame window for which you want the active sheet

functions.name: GetAlignment
functions.documentation: Obtains the alignment of the paragraph containing the insertion point in a RichTextEdit control.

params.name: rtename
params.description: The name of the RichTextEdit control in which you want to find out the alignment of the paragraph containing the insertion point

functions.name: GetApplication
functions.documentation: Gets the handle of the current Application object so you can get and set properties of the application.

functions.name: GetApplicationButton
functions.documentation: Gets the application button of the RibbonBar control.

params.name: controlname
params.description: The name of the RibbonBar control.

params.name: Item
params.description: A RibbonApplicationButtonItem variable in which you want to store the application button.

functions.name: GetArgElement
functions.documentation: Returns the value in the specified argument.

params.name: activexcontrol
params.description: Identifier for the instance of the PowerBuilder window ActiveX control. When used in HTML, the ActiveX control is the NAME attribute of the OBJECT element. When used in other environments, references the control that contains the PowerBuilder window ActiveX.

params.name: index
params.description: Integer specify the argument to return.

functions.name: GetAt

functions.name: GetDataStyle
functions.documentation: Finds out the appearance of a data point in a graph. Each data point in a series can have individual appearance settings. There are different syntaxes, depending on what settings you want to check. GetDataStyle provides information about a single data point. The series to which the data point belongs has its own style settings. In general, the style values for the data point are the same as its series' settings. Use SetDataStyle to change the style values for individual data points. Use GetSeriesStyle and SetSeriesStyle to get and set style information for the series. The graph stores style information for properties that do not apply to the current graph type. For example, you can find out the fill pattern for a data point or a series in a 2-dimensional line graph, but that fill pattern will not be visible. For the enumerated datatype values that GetDataStyle stores in linestyle and enumvariable, see SetDataStyle.

functions.name: GetFileOpenName
functions.documentation: Displays the system's Open File dialog box and allows the user to select a file or enter a file name.
functions.syntax: GetFileOpenName ( title, pathname, filename {, extension {, filter { , initdir { , aFlag } } } } ) GetFileOpenName ( title, pathname, filename[ ] {, extension {, filter { , initdir { , aFlag } } } } )

params.name: title
params.description: A string whose value is the title of the dialog box.

params.name: pathname
params.description: A string variable in which you want to store the returned path. If the user selects a single file, the pathname variable contains the path name and file name.

params.name: filename,
params.description: A string variable in which the returned file name is stored or an array of string variables in which multiple selected file names are stored. Specifying an array of string variables enables multiple selection in the dialog box.

params.name: extension
params.description: A string whose value is a 1- to 3-character default file extension. The default is no extension.

params.name: filter
params.description: A string whose value is a text description of the files to include in the list box and the file mask that you want to use to select the displayed files (for example, *.* or *.exe). The format for filter is: description,*. ext To specify multiple filter patterns for a single display string, use a semicolon to separate the patterns, for example: "Graphic Files (*.bmp;*.gif;*.jpg;*.jpeg), *.bmp;*.gif;*.jpg;*.jpeg" The default is: "All Files (*.*),*.*"

params.name: initdir
params.description: A string whose value is the initial directory name. The default is the current directory.

params.name: aFlag
params.description: An unsigned long whose value determines which options are enabled in the dialog box. The value of each option's flag is calculated as 2 to the power of (index -1), where index is the integer associated with the option. The value of the aggregate flag passed to GetFileOpenName is the sum of the individual option flags. See the table in the Usage section for a list of options, the index associated with each option, and the option's meaning.

params.name: objectname
params.description: The name of the RESTClient object from which you want to get the JWT token.

params.name: urlName
params.description: A string value specifying the URL.

params.name: data
params.description: A string value specifying the data to send. If the user sets the encoding charset in the Content-Type request header, this function will encode the data with the specified charset; if charset is not specified, this function will encode the data in UTF-8 by default.

params.name: token
params.description: The server response which contains the access token. If RESTClient failed to send request or server provides no response, the response value is an empty string. If the response value is compressed, it will be automatically decompressed. Gzip and Brotli compression formats are supported. If the server specified the Content-Type response header, and in which the encoding charset is specified, this function will encode the data with the specified charset; if charset is not specified, this function will encode the data in UTF-8 by default.

functions.name: GetSeriesStyle
functions.documentation: Finds out the appearance of a series in a graph. The appearance settings for individual data points can override the series settings, so the values obtained from GetSeriesStyle may not reflect the current state of the graph. There are several syntaxes, depending on what settings you want. GetSeriesStyle provides information about a series. The data points in the series can have their own style settings. Use SetSeriesStyle to change the style values for a series. Use GetDataStyle to get style information for a data point and SetDataStyle to override series settings and set style information for individual data points. The graph stores style information for properties that do not apply to the current graph type. For example, you can find out the fill pattern for a data point or a series in a two-dimensional line graph, but that fill pattern will not be visible.

params.name: controlname
params.description: The name of the graph in which you want to obtain the color of a series, or the name of the DataWindow control containing the graph.

params.name: graphcontrol
params.description: A string whose value is the name of the graph in the DataWindow control for which you want the color of a series.

params.name: seriesname
params.description: A string whose value is the name of the series for which you want the color.

params.name: colortype
params.description: A value of the grColorType enumerated datatype specifying the aspect of the series for which you want the color: Foreground! -- Text color Background! -- Background color LineColor! -- Line color Shade! -- Shade (for graphs that are 3-dimensional or have solid data markers)

params.name: colorvariable
params.description: A long variable in which you want to store the color's RGB value.

params.name: linestyle
params.description: A variable of type LineStyle in which you want to store the line style of seriesname.

params.name: linewidth
params.description: An integer variable in which you want to store the line width for seriesname. The width is measured in pixels.

params.name: enumvariable
params.description: The variable in which you want to store the style information. You can specify a FillPattern or grSymbolType variable. The style information that GetSeriesStyle stores depends on the variable type.

params.name: overlayindicator
params.description: A boolean variable in which you want to store a value indicating whether the series is an overlay. GetSeriesStyle sets overlayindicator to true if the series is an overlay and false if it is not.

functions.documentation: Gets the value of the key and inserts it into a DataWindow control, DataStore object, or DataWindowChild object. If more than one key with the same name exists, then get the value of the first key. Notice that the IgnoreCase property (true by default) determines whether the key name will be matched in a case-sensitive manner. This function will fail to import data properly, if the DataWindow is in query mode.
functions.syntax: objectname.GetValueToDataWindow (string key, dwcontrol DWControl {, boolean resetflag} {, string error} {, DWBuffer dwbuffer {, long startrow {, long endrow } } } )

params.name: objectname
params.description: The name of the JSONPackage object

params.name: Key
params.description: A string specifying the key of the item of JsonStringItem type. The key value is the JSON-formatted data which is in the format described in the section called “Supported JSON formats” in Application Techniques . If it is DataWindow JSON, GetValueToDataWindow will ignore the mapping-method element of the JSON data.

params.name: dwcontrol
params.description: A reference to a DataWindow control, DataStore, or DataWindowChild.

params.name: resetflag
params.description: A boolean value specifying whether dwcontrol should automatically reset the update flag. The default is TRUE.

params.name: error
params.description: A variable into which the returned warning or error message will be placed. When there are a large amount of error messages, the error information will only display the total number of errors, and the detailed message of the first 10 errors. The import warning caused by data type mismatch will not affect the return value of ImportJsonByKey; although the data of the mismatched columns will not be imported, the rest columns (even only one column) that are matched will be imported successfully; and that row will be regarded as a successful import and counted into the return value. The import error caused by DW presentation style mismatch, invalid arguments, startrow value greater than the number of rows,etc. will be regarded as a failure, and represented by a negative return value of GetValueToDataWindow, instead of being placed into this variable. See the Return Value section for more. Most of the messages placed into this variable are warnings (such as data type mismatch) rather than errors. Developers can adjust the JSON data according to the message or simply ignore the message if the problematic column is not critical and the corresponding DataWindow column can be left blank.

params.name: dwbuffer
params.description: A value of the dwBuffer enumerated datatype identifying the DataWindow buffer from which you want to import the data. For a list of valid values, see the section called “DWBuffer” in DataWindow Reference . For plain JSON: If not specified, imports the JSON data to the Primary! buffer. If specified, imports the JSON data to the specified buffer. For DataWindow JSON: If not specified, imports data of all of the buffers from the JSON string to the corresponding buffers and, if any, imports the data for DataWindowChild. If specified, imports data of the specified buffer from the JSON string to the corresponding buffer.

params.name: startrow
params.description: The number of the first detail object in the JSON Array that you want to import. The default is 1. If it is 0 or negative, 1 is used.

params.name: endrow
params.description: The number of the last detail object in the JSON Array that you want to import. The default is the rest of the objects. If it is 0 or negative, it indicates the rest of rows.
